title: Quantification of the effect of energy imbalance on bodyweight (Hall et al. 2011)
content: Hall KD et al., Lancet 2011 — Body-weight change in response to a change in energy intake is a DYNAMIC process, not a static linear calorie equation. As weight changes, total energy expenditure adapts (both resting and non-resting components shift with body mass and composition), so the same fixed calorie deficit does not keep producing the same rate of weight loss indefinitely — the rate slows as the body approaches a new equilibrium. A fixed '3500 kcal = 1 lb' rule-of-thumb does not hold over realistic timeframes; weight trajectories should be modeled as approaching a new steady state, not extrapolated linearly forever.

title: Quantification of the effect of energy imbalance on bodyweight (Hall et al. 2011)
content: Hall et al. 2011 — Product implication: an AI coach or calorie-target engine should not treat a prescribed deficit (e.g. -500 kcal/day) as producing a fixed, unchanging weekly weight-loss rate forever. Re-evaluate and adjust prescriptions periodically against OBSERVED trend data rather than a static formula projected far into the future. This is also the modeling basis later used by tools like the NIH Body Weight Planner — referencing that this reasoning exists is fine; claiming to have implemented the NIH model itself is not, unless it actually has been.
